Hans von Seeckt.fact: This was most clearly illustrated by Seeckt's role during the Kapp Putsch of March 1920.

Hans von Seeckt.fact: The putsch failed only after the government called for a general strike, which shut down the German economy.

Hans von Seeckt.fact: Ludendorff's right-hand man, Colonel Max Bauer asked Seeckt to become dictator; he refused contemptuously.

Hans von Seeckt.subject: Important Days
Hans von Seeckt.question: Seeckt's remark to the leaders of the republic, that "_____ do not fire on Reichswehr", was controversial
Hans von Seeckt.fact: Seeckt's remark to the leaders of the republic, that "Reichswehr do not fire on Reichswehr", was controversial.

Hans von Seeckt.subject: Important Days
Hans von Seeckt.question: His reserved attitude towards the _____ is illustrated by a brief conversation held with President Ebert
Hans von Seeckt.fact: His reserved attitude towards the Weimar Republic is illustrated by a brief conversation held with President Ebert.

Hans von Seeckt.subject: Important Days
Hans von Seeckt.question: In working to build a professional army within and without the confines of the Treaty of _____, Seeckt advanced the concept of the army as a "state-within-a-state"
Hans von Seeckt.fact: In working to build a professional army within and without the confines of the Treaty of Versailles, Seeckt advanced the concept of the army as a "state-within-a-state". This matched the conditions of the Versailles Treaty which were aimed at creating a long-term professional army with a ceiling of 100,000 volunteers and without significant reserves - a force which would not be able to challenge the much larger French Army.

Hans von Seeckt.fact: The control of the Arbeirakommandos was exercised through a group comprising Fedor von Bock, Kurt von Schleicher, Eugen Ott and Kurt von Hammerstein-Equord.

Hans von Seeckt.subject: Important Days
Hans von Seeckt.question: What came to be known as the _____" became infamous for its practice of using Feme murders to punish "traitors" who, for example, revealed the locations of weapons' stockpiles or names of members
Hans von Seeckt.fact: What came to be called the Black Reichswehr" became infamous for its practice of using Feme murders to punish "traitors" who, for example, revealed the locations of weapons' stockpiles or names of members.

Hans von Seeckt.subject: Important Days
Hans von Seeckt.question: During the trials of some of those charged with the murders, prosecutors alleged that the killings were ordered by the officers from _____'s group
Hans von Seeckt.fact: The control of the Arbeirakommandos was exercised through a group comprising Fedor von Bock, Kurt von Schleicher, Eugen Ott and Kurt von Hammerstein-Equord. During the trials of some of those charged with the murders, prosecutors alleged that the killings were ordered by the officers from Bock's group.

Hans von Seeckt.question: The GEFU founded factories in the _____ for the production of aircraft, tanks, artillery shells and poison gas

Hans von Seeckt.subject: Important Days
Hans von Seeckt.question: He saw _____ as a vassal state of France
Hans von Seeckt.fact: He saw Poland as a vassal state of France.

Hans von Seeckt.subject: Important Days
Hans von Seeckt.question: He felt a strong _____ would be a more attractive ally than a weak one
Hans von Seeckt.fact: He advocated strengthening Germany by whatever means were available, including reaching out to the Soviet Union. He felt a strong Germany would be a more attractive ally than a weak one.

Hans von Seeckt.subject: Important Days
Hans von Seeckt.question: The support between _____ and the Soviets was seen in this light, as an agreement that would add to the strength of both nations
Hans von Seeckt.fact: He advocated strengthening Germany by whatever means were available, including reaching out to the Soviet Union. He felt a strong Germany would be a more attractive ally than a weak one.

Hans von Seeckt.subject: Important Days
Hans von Seeckt.question: He did not believe such an agreement would alienate the _____
Hans von Seeckt.fact: He believed the United Kingdom would eventually be compelled to fight a war against its historic enemy, France, and that when such an event occurred the United Kingdom would be looking for an ally on the continent to carry the burden of a land war. He did not believe such an agreement would alienate the United Kingdom.

Hans von Seeckt.subject: Important Days
Hans von Seeckt.question: Seeckt's policies caused tension with the former _____ von Brockdorff-Rantzau, who was to be sent out as the Ambassador to Moscow
Hans von Seeckt.fact: Seeckt's policies caused tension with the former Foreign Minister Count Ulrich von Brockdorff-Rantzau, who was to be sent out as the Ambassador to Moscow.

Hans von Seeckt.subject: Important Days
Hans von Seeckt.question: Moreover, _____-Rantzau feared that a too close rapprochement with the Soviet Union would alienate Britain and drive her into the arms of France
Hans von Seeckt.fact: Seeckt's policies caused tension with the former Foreign Minister Count Ulrich von Brockdorff-Rantzau, who was to be sent out as the Ambassador to Moscow. Brockdorff-Rantzau was just as committed as Seeckt to the destruction of Versailles, but rather preferred to accomplish that goal through an alliance with Britain.

Hans von Seeckt.subject: Important Days
Hans von Seeckt.question: In response, on 11 September _____, Seeckt sent a memo to Brockdorff-Rantzau entitled "Germany's Attitude to the Russian Problem"
Hans von Seeckt.fact: In response, on 11 September 1922, Seeckt sent a memo to Brockdorff-Rantzau entitled "Germany's Attitude to the Russian Problem".

Hans von Seeckt.fact: In response, on 11 September 1922, Seeckt sent a memo to Brockdorff-Rantzau entitled "Germany's Attitude to the Russian Problem". Some of Seeckt's salient points were:Germany must pursue a policy of action.

Hans von Seeckt.subject: Important Days
Hans von Seeckt.question: This association between _____ and Russia is the first and almost the only increase in power which we have so far obtained since peace was made

This association between Germany and Russia is the first and almost the only increase in power which we have so far obtained since peace was made.

Hans von Seeckt.fact: The question of orientation towards the West, as far as France is concerned is ruled out … England is drifting towards another historic conflict with France, even through she does not face imminent war.

Hans von Seeckt.fact: A glance at the East is surely sufficient even for those who before Genoa did not wish to use their eyes and ears.

Hans von Seeckt.question: The moment is coming, and must come, when _____ will be looking for allies on the Continent
Hans von Seeckt.fact: The British interests in the Dardanelles, Egypt and India are certainly infinitely more important at the moment than those on the Rhine, and an understanding between Britain and France at Germany's expense, that is, a concession by Britain in return for an immediate advantage, is by no means improbable. The moment is coming, and must come, when Britain will be looking for allies on the Continent.

Hans von Seeckt.fact: War on the Rhine between France and Russia is a political bogy. It is echoed by many bourgeois-pacifist elements, but among the workers, and also among the members of the official Social Democratic Party there are many who are not prepared to eat out of the hands of France and Poland.

Hans von Seeckt.fact: A large military barracks in Celle was built in 1935 and named after von Seeckt.
